channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia deepen bilateral ties, RTV reports
item.description: Serbian media outlet RTV highlighted the growing relationship between Uzbekistan and Serbia, encompassing political dialogue, inter-parliamentary ties, cultural exchange, and trade-economic cooperation. The report noted that bilateral relations are elevating to a multifaceted partnership, based on mutual respect and national interest.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances judicial aid quality with increased judge numbers and reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly improved judicial assistance quality by increasing the number of judges from 1,057 in 2016 to 1,731 currently, despite population growth to 39 million. Reforms include establishing a unified Supreme Court and creating administrative courts to handle appeals against state bodies.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Family-Centric Approach to Poverty Reduction
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing a family-based approach to poverty reduction, focusing on individual family needs and circumstances. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need for targeted solutions beyond simple financial aid, encouraging entrepreneurship and stable income generation through practical support and skill development.

item.title: Tajikistan's 35th Independence Anniversary Celebrated with Reception in London
item.description: An official reception marking Tajikistan's 35th Independence Day was held in London on September 4, 2026, initiated by the Embassy of Tajikistan to the UK. The event featured an exhibition of national products and a cultural corner, with participation from UK government officials, diplomats, and members of the Tajik diaspora.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes prison sentences for damaging border fences
item.description: A bill submitted for public discussion in Kyrgyzstan proposes criminal liability for intentional damage to state border infrastructure. The draft law suggests two to five years in prison for damaging engineering structures and barriers. Authors argue such damage weakens border protection and can facilitate unauthorized crossings. Approximately 320 kilometers of barriers are installed along the Kyrgyz-Tajik border.

item.title: Iran warns of more painful response amid renewed US tensions
item.description: Iranian leadership has warned the United States of a more painful response amid renewed military tensions between Tehran and Washington. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged the US to properly assess the situation. The report indicates a potential escalation of military confrontations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Labor Minister dismissed, acting minister appointed
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev has been appointed acting head of the ministry and his candidacy will be submitted to parliament for approval. Imangaziev, a career diplomat with a PhD in political science, previously served as Deputy Foreign Minister.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor Kanat Sagynbayev dismissed, Almaz Imangaziev appointed acting head
item.description: Kanat Sagynbayev has been dismissed as the Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration of Kyrgyzstan. Almaz Imangaziev has been appointed acting head of the ministry and his candidacy will be submitted to the Jogorku Kenesh for approval. Imangaziev previously served as Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Gazprom increases gas exports to Central Asia by 70 percent since early 2026
item.description: Gazprom has increased its gas exports to Central Asia by 70 percent since the beginning of 2026, according to company head Alexey Miller. Deliveries to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan have approached this growth mark. Kyrgyzstan requires nearly half a billion cubic meters of gas annually, with long-term contracts extending to 2040.

item.title: Tajikistan's Salos CJSC begins construction of new oil processing line
item.description: Salos CJSC in Tajikistan's Jayhun district has started building a new oil processing line with a capacity of 50,000 tons per year. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources reported that the new line will enable the production of diesel fuel and gasoline, expanding the company's product range beyond bitumen. The project is timed to coincide with the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence.

item.title: Baku to host the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue
item.description: Baku, Azerbaijan will host the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue from October 27-29, 2026. The forum, organized in partnership with UNESCO, the UN Alliance of Civilizations, ISESCO, and UN Tourism, aims to foster dialogue between peoples, religions, and communities. This year marks the 15th anniversary of the forum, initiated by Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev in 2008.

item.title: Uzbekistan reallocates public security functions between police units
item.description: Uzbekistan is reallocating certain functions and powers between internal affairs bodies to improve public security. Starting November 1, 2026, patrol units will respond to emergency calls via the '112' system. Patrol and security services will also gain new powers in traffic management, including clearing congestion on main streets and around key locations.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Patrol Inspectors to Gain Authority to Punish Traffic Violations
item.description: Patrol inspectors in Uzbekistan will be granted additional authority to issue punishments for certain traffic violations. Administrative responsibility will also be established for obstructing their official duties.

item.title: Uzbek citizen who fought for Russia in Ukraine sentenced to two years
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, F.A., who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict, has been sentenced to two years in prison in Namangan, Uzbekistan. He was recruited while serving a drug sentence in Russia and participated in combat operations before being injured by a drone. He later obtained Russian citizenship and returned to Uzbekistan.

item.title: Man arrested in Tajikistan for assaulting and threatening to kill a canteen employee
item.description: A man, Nurmurodzoda Zakhriddin, has been arrested in Zafarabad district, Tajikistan, for assaulting and threatening to kill an employee of the "Hayid" canteen. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that the incident occurred on August 19, 2026, while the man was intoxicated. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Uzbekistan Appoints First Ambassador to Syria, Based in Kuwait
item.description: Ayubkhon Yunusov has presented his credentials as Uzbekistan's first ambassador to Syria to Syrian Foreign Minister Asad Hasan ash-Shayboni. The ambassador is based in Kuwait. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral ties, including establishing a joint economic committee and political consultations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Export Berries and Fruits to China Following Phytosanitary Protocol Signing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will export berries and fruits, including raspberries, blackberries, and currants, to China. A phytosanitary protocol was signed within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization framework, expanding export opportunities beyond traditional EAEU markets and potentially boosting domestic berry cultivation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan School Enrollment: One Week Left for First Grade Registration
item.description: Approximately 143,300 children have been enrolled in first grade in Kyrgyzstan's schools, with Bishkek registering 25,400. Osh has enrolled 10,600 children. Electronic registration began April 1, and parents must submit medical certificates for admitted students. The academic year starts September 15.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to build new water supply systems in three regions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is implementing a program to provide 130 villages in Osh, Chuy, and Issyk-Kul regions with safe drinking water and modern sanitation. Over 450,000 residents will gain access to clean water. Specialized municipal enterprises are being established to manage these new water supply and sanitation services.

item.title: US envoys discuss war end conditions with Zelensky in Kyiv
item.description: US special envoy Stephen Wittekoff and advisor Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv to discuss potential conditions for ending the war. They also discussed short-term Western support and security guarantees for Ukraine. Zelensky indicated the war might continue through winter, requesting winter aid.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Japarov meets Tatarstan Head Minnikhanov
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov met with Rustam Minnikhanov, Head of Tatarstan, in Cholpon-Ata. They discussed trade and economic cooperation, noting a significant increase in mutual trade turnover. Cooperation also extends to biodiversity conservation, specifically snow leopard population preservation.

item.title: US proposes peace plan for Ukraine involving troop withdrawal and referendums
item.description: Ukrainian media reports a US peace plan proposing Ukraine withdraw troops from parts of Donbas, with Russia pledging not to deploy forces there. The plan includes a UN-controlled buffer zone, referendums in certain regions, constitutional changes, and Ukraine's non-bloc status. US envoys called talks in Moscow 'substantive'.

item.title: Global sugar and grain prices rise, impacting Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.9% in August due to adverse weather, Black Sea logistics issues, and Middle East tensions, with sugar and grains seeing significant price hikes. Sugar prices jumped 11.9% due to drought in Europe and El Niño effects. Grain prices increased 2.2%, with wheat up 2.6%.

item.title: Uzbekistan's beef imports increased by 23% in August
item.description: Uzbekistan's beef imports rose by 23% in August compared to the previous month. The country purchased the largest amount of beef from abroad since the beginning of the year during August.

item.title: UN Human Rights Council session begins in Geneva, addressing global rights situations
item.description: The 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council commenced in Geneva, with 47 member states set to review human rights globally. Discussions will include Afghanistan, Syria, Myanmar, Sudan, Belarus, Iran, and Ukraine, alongside other crisis situations and specific territorial issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees 22% rise in incarceration over six months, with 11,700 sentenced
item.description: The number of people sentenced to imprisonment in Uzbekistan increased by 22% in the first six months of the year, totaling 11,700 individuals. Two individuals from Tashkent received life sentences.

item.title: German Public Growing Trust in AfD Party Amidst Government Crisis, Poll Shows
item.description: German public trust in the AfD party is increasing due to dissatisfaction with the government's performance, according to DW. A September "ARD-Deutschlandtrend" poll indicates 84% are unhappy with the federal government. The AfD leads polls at 27%, significantly ahead of the CDU/CSU's 21%.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Islamic Civilization Center Need Distinct International Voice, Says BBC Representative
item.description: Uzbekistan and its Center for Islamic Civilization must develop their own international voice, according to Sergey Stanovkin, BBC Studios' Eurasia commercial representative. The recent International Media Forum in Tashkent, attended by global media, aimed to enhance Uzbekistan's presence in the international information space and showcase its culture and history.

item.title: CCA Tashkent Opens as Central Asia's First Comprehensive Contemporary Art Center
item.description: The Center for Contemporary Art (CCA) Tashkent has opened, featuring exhibition halls, a library, concept store, and educational spaces. Housed in a historic 1912 power station, it's Central Asia's first institution of its kind. Saida Mirziyoyeva highlighted its role in promoting Uzbek artists internationally.

item.title: 83% of Uzbek university graduates employed, new 'Graduate Quality Index' developed
item.description: A study in Uzbekistan reveals that 83% of university graduates are employed. The country has developed a new "Graduate Quality Index" to analyze graduate employment rates, income, and speed of job placement. The findings were published on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Central Asia-China Political Party Dialogue Conference Held in Samarkand
item.description: A conference on the "Role of Political Parties in Strengthening Ties between Central Asian Countries and China" took place in Samarkand. Representatives from political parties of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan, along with a Chinese Communist Party delegation, attended. The dialogue aims to enhance strategic trust and multilateral cooperation between the regions.

item.title: Young Parliamentarians Convene in Samarkand for Global Conference
item.description: Young parliamentarians from 60 countries and 13 international organizations gathered in Samarkand for the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians. The event, initiated by Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, focused on restoring human rights, justice, and dignity in challenging times. Delegates shared experiences and sought common solutions to global issues, emphasizing youth participation.

item.title: World Nomad Games becoming comparable to Olympics, World Cup, says Kyrgyz PM
item.description: Kyrgyzstan handed over the World Nomad Games baton to Russia, with the next edition set for Tatarstan in 2028. Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev stated the games have become a major international cultural and sports movement, comparable to the Olympics and World Cup.

item.title: Uzbekistan U-20 team qualifies for U-20 Asian Cup after defeating Syria
item.description: Uzbekistan's youth national team secured a spot in the U-20 Asian Cup by defeating Syria with a large score. The tournament will be held in China from March 24 to April 10, 2027. Semi-finalists will qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

item.title: Uzbekistan Opens Consulate General in Seattle, USA
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially opened its Consulate General in Seattle, Washington, marking the country's first consular presence in the U.S. Pacific Northwest. The new consulate aims to strengthen trade, economic, investment, technological, educational, and humanitarian ties between Uzbekistan and the United States. Its consular district covers Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Montana.

item.title: 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians Held Successfully in Samarkand
item.description: The 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians, themed 'For Human Rights, Justice, and Dignity in a Complex World,' was successfully held in Samarkand from September 4-6. The event was organized by the Inter-Parliamentary Union.

item.title: New International Airline May Be Established in Uzbekistan in Partnership with Afghanistan
item.description: A new international airline could be established in Uzbekistan in cooperation with Afghanistan. This possibility was discussed in the Fergana region with the head of Kam Air, focusing on available opportunities and necessary infrastructure.

item.title: Criminal Cases in Uzbekistan Courts Increased by 29% in Six Months
item.description: The number of criminal cases heard in Uzbekistan's courts rose by 29% in the first six months of the year. The proportion of grave crimes increased by 18%, and particularly grave crimes by 19%, with the capital seeing the most offenses.

item.title: Uzbek President's Belgrade visit aims to strengthen ties and foster practical cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's upcoming visit to Serbia signifies a new phase in bilateral relations, building on historical Silk Road connections. Both nations express readiness to enhance partnership, with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić calling the visit a "powerful impetus" for development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President and Tatarstan Head Discuss Cooperation and World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov met with Tatarstan Head Rustam Minnikhanov in Cholpon-Ata. They discussed trade and economic cooperation, with bilateral trade exceeding $182 million last year. Japarov pledged support for the 2028 World Nomad Games in Kazan.
